questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 21 cm and a height of 6 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 21 × 6 = 63 cm². Say the ½ out loud before multiplying so you don't skip it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an open dish, burning wood seems to lose mass. Where did that mass actually go?
questions.why: Mass isn't destroyed — gases produced by burning escape into the air and aren't weighed, so the system only looks lighter.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What word describes a solid that suddenly forms when two liquids react together?
questions.why: A precipitate is a solid that suddenly appears when two solutions react — a clear visible sign a chemical change has happened.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: A snack ad shows teenagers laughing together at a party while eating chips. What technique is this?
questions.why: Showing happy teens at a party links the snack to fitting in and having fun — an appeal to belonging, not any fact about the food's nutrition.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, which nutrient is usually the highest in a packet of chips?
questions.why: Chips are usually highest in fat, since fat packs more energy per gram than protein or carbs. Students often assume protein or fibre dominates savoury snacks when fat is really the main contributor.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When two substances react and form a new substance, what has actually changed?
questions.why: In a chemical reaction, atoms don't disappear — their bonds break and rearrange into new substances, which is why the properties change.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: Why might grilled chicken be a healthier pick than fried chicken?
questions.why: Frying adds extra oil, raising the fat content well above grilling. Protein stays roughly the same either way, so that's not the real difference.
